I worked at this park when I was a teenager. I'll give you a story I wrote for when this was posted elsewhere.

Well, I was 17 and a lead for an area called Roaring Springs. It had rides like the single and double tubes, the alpine water tunnel and our most notoriously dangerous, The Aqua Scoot.

The Aqua Scoot was a large ramp made of rollers that guests would slide down on a plastic sled. At the bottom of the ramp was a long pool they would glide over or crash into.

The problems arose when the instructions by the guard on top where either ignored or not understood. Action Park was so popular at the time because it chartered buses directly from NYC. So we got a lot of guests that spoke little or no English.

We knew the ride was potentially dangerous so every guard on top of the ride gave the same speach. When we encountered a guest that didn't understand the conversation went like this:

Guard-"place your cart on the rollers, now sit on it and hold the handles tightly. No matter what do not let go or lean back.

Customer-"yes, yes"

Guard- (suspicious the guest doesn't speak English) "do you understand what I just explained?"

Guest- "yes, yes"

Guard- "are you from Jupiter?"

Guest- "yes, yes"

Guard now convinced the guest doesn't understand tries to mime the instructions as best as they can.

Guard pushes cart down the rollers

Guest careens down rollers picking up speed

Guest reaches transition of ramp

Guest leans back

Guest smacks head on rollers

Carnage ensues.

As I see it, the rebels were trying to shoot down Ukrainian military planes which were flying in the area. Due to their lack of proper equipment and training, they were unable to distinguish the targets with any degree of precision and fired at what they saw. It stands to reason that they would not have been expecting civilian aircraft to fly over an active war zone. It also stands to reason that civilian aircraft should not have been allowed to fly over an active war zone. So the rebels accidentally shot down the plane, at first thinking they had shot down a transport plane (which was flying in the area at the time and was targeted and hit by their fire). When they arrived on scene, there was naturally a lot of confusion and they were understandably in denial that they had just shot down a civilian airliner, because why would it be in the area? Their first reaction was naturally to pass the blame to their enemies. Their enemy's first reaction was naturally to say they did it on purpose.

So the rebels did it, but not on purpose. They own that share of the blame. The Ukrainian government and the airline share the other part of the blame for putting the plane in harms way, and not even knowing that it would be in harms way, which there's no excuse for. I don't see how Russia or any other party could share blame for this without proving that Russia's government gave the rebels the tools with which they made this mistake. The rebels could easily have stolen such weaponry from the Ukrainian military. There are some questions still about why the plane was rerouted to the area, and providing cover to military aircraft is a possibility (maybe they thought the rebels wouldn't shoot if they knew civilian aircraft was in the area... which unfortunately they did not know or were not able to know). So yeah, it's complicated, and people don't like complicated.
